summary: Two wooden lights were first shown on Plum Island in 1788; the present white tower dates from 1898. Automated 1951; City of Newburyport owns it, Friends run tours.

lens.where: NRHP (1981) says an automatic plastic lens replaced the Fresnel lens. The Friends' website says the Coast Guard still maintains the Fresnel lens, and the USLHS record lists a fourth-order Fresnel as the current optic. Unresolved; status left unknown.

structures.note: Conical white tower, shingled (NRHP; LighthouseFriends calls it a 45-foot wooden conical tower).
Front range tower burned after lightning struck it on 8 August 1856 (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Grounds open. The tower is opened on Friends of Plum Island Light tour days, booked online.

facts.agency: City of Newburyport (owner); Friends of Plum Island Light (tours)

events.note: Lit 14 April 1788 (LighthouseFriends); the nomination dates the two wooden lights to 1788.
Lights ceded to the federal government (NRHP).
New Fresnel lenses (NRHP); a fifth-order Fresnel in the rear tower (LighthouseFriends).
Front range tower struck by lightning and burned, 8 August 1856; not replaced (LighthouseFriends).
A fourth-order Fresnel replaced the fifth-order lens (LighthouseFriends).
Towers moved 75 feet south (NRHP). LighthouseFriends says the towers moved north over the years; the sources conflict.
Front light changed from lard oil to mineral oil; a stone tower begun and never completed (NRHP). LighthouseFriends dates the mineral oil change to 1877.
Newburyport Harbor Range (front) discontinued in September 1890 (Board FY1891; the day is damaged in the OCR). LighthouseFriends gives 30 September 1890.
Channels shifted; construction on the stone tower halted; jetties built (NRHP).
A brick oil house was built at the station (Board FY1894).
Present white conical tower built (NRHP). The nomination says it may incorporate parts of an 1788 tower.
Light moved to a new tower 18 feet southeast on 20 September 1898 (Board FY1899; LighthouseFriends gives the same date).
Changed from oil to electric incandescent (Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1922). LighthouseFriends gives 1927 for electricity.
Automated; the Coast Guard disposed of surplus land around the keeper's dwelling (USLHS; NRHP; LighthouseFriends).

A fully automatic plastic lens replaced the Fresnel lens (NRHP). The Friends' website says the Coast Guard still maintains the Fresnel lens; the USLHS record lists a fourth-order Fresnel as the current optic. Unresolved.
Coast Guard leased the light to the Friends of Plum Island Light; ceremony 15 June 1996.
Coast Guard deeded the lighthouse and property to the City of Newburyport.
Fence built to enclose about two acres around the light-house buildings (Board, report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1896).
Lights moved one third of a mile northeast, as close to the channel as possible (NRHP).

wrecks.outcome: Wrecked in the gale; the captain's wife was swept away and drowned. Keeper George, away from the light, could not return and the lights were left dark (LighthouseFriends).

corrections.why: The nomination says an automatic plastic lens replaced the Fresnel lens in 1981, so the order-4 Fresnel is not recorded as in place. Where it went is not in the sources read.

The standing conical tower dates from 1898 (Board FY1899: light moved to a new tower on 20 September 1898). The 1788 towers were replaced; the nomination says the new tower may incorporate parts of one.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1788 is the first pair of towers. The present tower was built in 1898, and the light was moved to it on 20 September 1898 (Board FY1899). The nomination says it may incorporate parts of an 1788 tower.
The Board's FY1891 report lists the front range light among lights discontinued in September 1890; the day is damaged in the OCR. LighthouseFriends gives 30 September 1890.

notes_for_editor: FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22 (independent check; story and this record revised). UNRESOLVED CONFLICTS: (1) The 1788 pair: NRHP calls them the eleventh lighthouse built in the U.S.; LighthouseFriends says thirteenth. (2) Tower: NRHP gives a 50-foot white shingled tower (cylindrical in its description, conical in its chronology); LighthouseFriends gives a 45-foot wooden conical tower; the record has 13.5 m. (3) Electricity: Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1922 lists Newburyport Harbor as changed to electric incandescent; LighthouseFriends gives 1927. (4) Mineral oil in the front light: NRHP gives 1887; LighthouseFriends gives 1877. (5) Moves: NRHP gives 1869 (one third of a mile northeast) and 1874 (75 feet south); LighthouseFriends says the towers moved north over the years, about 3,000 feet in all. (6) Friends of Plum Island Light: founded 1994 per the Friends' website; 1995 per LighthouseFriends. (7) Lens: NRHP says an automatic plastic lens replaced the Fresnel lens in 1981; the Friends' website says the Coast Guard still maintains the Fresnel lens; the USLHS record lists a fourth-order Fresnel as the current optic. Status left unknown. (8) The Board's FY1891 entry (Lights discontinued, scan p.18): the day is damaged in the OCR ('September .'$0, 1890'); the story says September 1890 and gives LighthouseFriends's 30 September. (9) Fence: the entry (scan p.58) is in the report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1896. The corpus label 1896-1897 covers the FY1897 report too; the story and sources now cite FY1896. OCR TABLE CHECKS: the 1926 Bulletin salary line 'At Plum Island, Mr. Lowell, with ditto ... 220.00' (PDF page 13; page 15 gives 220 for the same line) was read from the printed line text, not by column position. ROSTER: matched by name to USLHS plum-island-ma, whose position is 1.8 km from the station's (USLHS positions are only to the minute); the 20 roster lines match the record. NEWSPAPERS: none used (one 1894 Chronicling America page is for Plum Island off Connecticut). LF-ONLY FACTS, no primary record read: the 1787 approval and 1788 lighting dates, the Lowell family details, the 1808 whirlwind and 1809 appropriation, the 1839 gale and Richmond Packet wreck (the Niles' passage is second-hand through LighthouseFriends), the 1842 inspection quotation, the 1856 lightning, the 1871 lens change, the 1898 telephone line, the 1927 electricity date and the 1995 Friends formation. Check them against primary records before publication. The Life-Saving Service station at Plum Island is a separate station record and is not covered here.
